focus_areas.area: Root account protection (MFA, access keys, usage)
IAM user and role security (aging credentials, unused access)
External identity federation and trust relationships
Cross-account access and assume role chains

rule.title: Root Account Critical
rule.description: Root account findings are ALWAYS Critical if credentials are active
rule.action: Flag any root access keys, root MFA absence, or root console usage

rule.title: Credential Age
rule.description: Access keys older than 90 days are High/Medium depending on usage

rule.title: Privilege Escalation
rule.description: Policies allowing iam:* or sts:AssumeRole without restrictions are Critical
rule.action: Analyze inline and attached policies for overly permissive grants

rule.title: MFA Enforcement
rule.description: Users with console access MUST have MFA enabled
rule.metric: Check MFADevices array is non-empty for console users

rule.title: Unused Access
rule.description: Users with no recent activity (>90 days) should be disabled or removed

focus.check: Root user existence and credential status
Access key creation dates and last used dates
Trust chain depth and cross-account access
Inline policies with wildcard permissions (iam:*, s3:*)

steps.step: 1. Sign in as root or use IAM user with root permissions
2. Navigate to Security Credentials in AWS Console
4. Create IAM users with delegated permissions instead
5. Verify MFA is enabled on root account
1. Review the policy statement allowing iam:* or Action: "*"
4. Add conditions if applicable (IP restrictions, MFA requirement)
5. Test with affected user/role to ensure functionality
